reason: This passage (Exodus 2:1-10) does not depict any conflict at all. The text is a personal, familial narrative focused on the birth of Moses and his rescue by Pharaoh's daughter. The interaction between the Egyptian princess and the Hebrew child is characterized by compassion (וַתַּחְמֹ֣ל עָלָ֔יו - 'she had compassion on him') and care, not conflict. While the broader Exodus narrative involves national/peoplehood tensions, this specific fragment is entirely individualized and non-conflictual.
